newsitem.title: INDIA: Militants kill six people in northeast India.
newsitem.headline: Militants kill six people in northeast India.

text.p: Six people were killed in India's northeastern region in scattered incidents of violence, and separatists led a general strike coinciding with independence day celebrations, police said on Friday.
Separatist guerrillas shot four people dead in three overnight attacks in Assam state, police in the region's biggest city, Guwahati, told Reuters.
Separatist militants also blew up a bridge in the central section of the state and set fire to a small railway station on the main track connecting the region with the rest of India, they said.
Tribal guerrillas killed two Bengali-speaking Hindus at Teliamura in Tripura on Thursday night, police said.

Six separatist groups in Tripura, Assam, Manipur and Nagaland states called last month for a general strike on Independence Day and a boycott of celebrations marking 50 years of freedom from British rule.
Two tribal groups demanding that separate provinces be carved out of Manipur and Tripura joined the strike.
Two bomb blasts also rocked Nagaland, but no one was injured, the Press Trust of India (PTI) said.
One of the explosions occurred minutes after state Chief Minister S.C. Jamir gave an Independence Day speech.
"Life is normal in all parts of the state," Nepal Das, a senior police official told Reuters at Agartala, Tripura's capital. He said paramilitary troops had been deployed throughout the state.

More than 200 ethnic groups, each with its own guerrilla forces, are fighting for homelands in the hilly, heavily wooded northeast. The tribal groups have uneasy relations with settlers from the plains, mainly Bengali speaking Hindus.
Authorities imposed tight security on a ceremony in Guwahati commemorating India's independence, deploying soldiers and paramilitary troopers on rooftops.
Residents were not allowed to open their doors or windows until the end of the event, which went off peacefully, and dignitaries had left the site of the flag-raising.
The Maoist United Liberation Front of Asom (ULFA), which accuses New Delhi of neglecting the region's economic development, had called for a "curfew" until noon (0630 GMT) on Friday.

On Thursday, seven people were killed and eight injured when a bomb planted by suspected separatists exploded on a train track about 200 km (120 miles) east of Guwahati, derailing a passenger carriage.

In Jammu and Kashmir, a major area of separatist violence in India, the All-Parties Hurriyat (Freedom) Conference imposed a "civil curfew" to protest against Indian authorities, but there were no reports of violence.
Shops and businesses were closed in Srinagar, the state capital, and in major towns in response to the strike called by Moslem separatists, police and witnesses said.
"On Friday, we will mourn the death and destruction which 50 years of India's independence has brought us," the Hurriyat, which groups 30 religious and political groups, said in a statement.
Police and hospitals say more than 20,000 people have died since a violent separatist rebellion began in the state, which is mainly Hindu India's only Moslem majority province.
